title: Map Studio
toolPaintHint: Paint with the chosen terrain; choose Sea to erase land
toolTerrainHint: Change the terrain on land only; the coastline stays put
toolFillHint: Replace a connected area of one terrain with the chosen terrain
landBrushSmall: Small brush: the land you draw is thin and its provinces come out long and narrow; patches under 8 pixels go back to sea when saved.
natural: Natural edges (coastlines are not perfect circles)
hints: Left-click to paint · Right-drag or hold Space to move the map · Scroll to zoom · Ctrl+Z to undo · [ ] for brush size · Esc to leave
countriesEmpty: No countries yet: add or create one in the panel on the right.
toolCountryHint: Paint the chosen country onto land (not the sea)
toolCountryFillHint: Paint a whole connected landmass with the chosen country
toolEraseHint: Remove the country; the terrain stays
startIntro: Pick a starting point, then change it with the tools on the left. Switching starts can be undone too.
countriesIntro: Choose the countries of this world (up to {max}), then paint them onto the land with the country brush on the left.
longTags: {count} countries are not listed: their tags are not three characters, and the game map only takes three-character tags.
unpainted: {share}% of the land is not painted: on save it goes to the nearest country.
notPainted: {names} has no land painted yet: it would get no state, so building stops.
removeBody: Its land becomes unpainted. This cannot be undone, and the undo history is cleared.
notBase: The project map has already been changed (new land, province edits, or a new world), so it cannot be replaced directly. Undo it or restore the base map in the World Map workbench first.
sizeHint: Fine = as many provinces as the base game (takes longer); Coarse = big provinces and few states, good for a first try.
seed: Layout (another number divides the provinces differently)
generating: Dividing provinces, states and strategic regions, about 10 seconds…
previewHint: When the terrain and countries are painted, click Build preview: the result is laid right over the map.
stale: The draft changed: build the preview again before saving.
summary: {land} land provinces · {sea} sea provinces · {states} states · {regions} strategic regions
confirm: I understand this replaces the whole world (it can be undone in the World Map workbench)
saveNote: Once saved, the GameView map is the world you painted.
needCountries: Add at least one country under Countries first
waitNotBase: The project map was already changed: undo it in the World Map workbench first
waitBlocked: The checks found errors: fix the draft and build again
waitConfirm: Tick the confirmation above to save
editKind: Changing the map you have · Only you see it here until you save
editIntro: Pick a country and paint provinces over to it with the brush; fill a whole area at once, or erase land to blank. Switch to Terrain, Rivers or Land and the same tools change terrain, draw rivers, or paint new land on the sea. Changes only show here until you click Save. A state painted only in part is cut: the painted provinces join the state of the new owner next to them, or become a new state of their own.
toolBrushHint: Hold the left button and paint: every province you brush goes to the chosen country
paletteEmpty: No country chosen yet: add one below, or click the map with the picker.
editHints: Left-click to paint · Right-drag or hold Space to move the map · Scroll to zoom · B brush · E eraser · G fill · I picker · N new country · Alt-click to pick a country · [ ] brush size · Ctrl+Z to undo · Esc to leave
addCores: Also make them cores of the new owner
addCoresHint: With cores, the states count as core territory of the new owner in the game; existing cores stay.
savedChangesBody: You can undo this save from the panel.
discardBody: These provinces go back to their countries.
newWorldLink: Want to paint a whole new world from scratch? (replaces the entire map)
modLink: Have a MOD with its own map? Import it from the MOD's folder (replaces the entire map)
modIntro: Pick a MOD's folder (the one holding its map and history folders). Its provinces, states and strategic regions become the project's map as they are, in place of the current one. You can undo it.
modNoMap: No map (map/provinces.bmp) in this folder. Pick the MOD's own folder.
modWhich: This folder holds several MODs. Which one to import:
modFoundPictures: {count, plural, one {# map picture} other {# map pictures}}
modFoundStates: {count, plural, one {# state file} other {# state files}}
modFoundRegions: {count, plural, one {# strategic region file} other {# strategic region files}}
modFoundNames: {count, plural, one {# localisation file} other {# localisation files}} (only those naming states, regions and towns are read)
modReading: Reading the folder… a big MOD takes a moment
modScanCancelled: Scan cancelled. You can pick a folder again.
modScanLocal: This step only reads the files. Nothing has been changed yet.
modScanBrowser: Reading the file list. Scan progress will appear when the list is ready.
modScanned: {count, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} scanned
modReadFailed: Some files could not be read. Pick the folder again
fixedPixels: {count, plural, one {# pixel} other {# pixels}} that belonged to no province merged into the provinces around them
fixedLakeStates: {count, plural, one {# state} other {# states}} of only lakes given a land province
modMissing: Missing: {files}. They are needed to import the map as it is; pick the MOD's own folder.
modCountriesTitle: Countries of the MOD the project does not have
modCountriesHint: For each: make a country with the same tag, or merge it into one of the project's countries.
modMakeFailed: Could not make country {tag}. Create it in the countries workbench, or merge it into a project country instead.
modMissingFirst: The folder lacks files the import needs
modChooseCountries: First choose what to do with the MOD's countries the project does not have
modConfirm: I understand the import replaces the project's map and all its states, and unloads the base game's countries and history (it can be undone in the world map workbench)
modSaveNote: After the import you can keep editing in the map studio, or undo it in the world map workbench.
modStageHint: Pick a MOD's folder and preview it to see the imported map here.
newWorldKind: The whole world redrawn · The draft is kept on this computer
backToMap: ← Back to changing the map you have
undoneSave: Undone: {count} provinces are back as they were
toolEraserHint: Erase land to blank; on save it goes to the countries around it. Shift-click to erase a whole country
toolBucketHint: Click: the joined land of that country goes to the chosen country. Shift-click for the whole country
toolPickerHint: Click: pick the country there. With any other tool, Alt-click does the same
newCountryQuickHint: Make a new country right away and paint with it (N)
colorHint: Click the swatch to change the colour
erasedNote: {count} provinces are blank: on save they go to the countries around them
countryFailed: Could not create the new country “{name}”: {detail}
terrainBrushHint: Hold the left button and paint: the land provinces you brush take the chosen terrain
terrainEraserHint: Wipe painted terrain off: provinces go back to the terrain they had
terrainBucketHint: Click: the joined land of one terrain all takes the chosen terrain
terrainPickerHint: Click: pick the terrain there. With any other tool, Alt-click does the same
terrainHints: Left-click to paint · Right-drag or hold Space to move the map · Scroll to zoom · B brush · E eraser · G fill · I picker · Alt-click to pick a terrain · [ ] brush size · Ctrl+Z to undo · Esc to leave
terrainLook: Also change how the map looks: mountains rise, the ground colour and trees follow
terrainLookHint: Unticked, only the terrain the game counts changes (movement, supply, combat). Ticked, these provinces also get their ground, height, colour and trees redrawn, the way the base game draws that terrain.
riverBrushHint: Hold the left button and draw from the source downstream: reach the sea and that is its mouth; reach another river and it becomes a tributary
riverEraserHint: Rivers you brush are wiped whole, with the tributaries flowing into them
riverHints: Left-click to draw a river · Right-drag or hold Space to move the map · Scroll to zoom (rivers are one pixel wide; zoom in to see them) · B draw · E erase · [ ] eraser size · Ctrl+Z to undo · Esc to leave
riverUnavailable: Could not read the river map: {detail}
riverNote_blocked: It cannot join here: a tributary must meet a plain stretch of river from the side, not next to a source or another junction
riverNote_start: A river cannot start here: begin on land with no river on it or beside it
riverNote_short: Too short: a river needs at least three pixels
landBrushHint: Hold the left button and paint new land on the sea (only the sea takes it); saving cuts it into provinces and states
landEraserHint: Wipe new land that is not saved yet
landHints: Left-click to paint on the sea · Right-drag or hold Space to move the map · Scroll to zoom · B brush · E eraser · [ ] brush size · Ctrl+Z to undo · Esc to leave
landTooBig: The new land is too large (at most about 2048×1024 pixels): paint it in parts
savingLand: Making the new land, this takes a while…
lakeBrushHint: Land provinces you brush become lakes, whole
lakeEraserHint: Take back lakes that are not saved yet
lakeWholeState: {state} would be drowned whole: a state must keep at least one province
lakeNote: Whole provinces become lakes. Their victory points, buildings, railways and supply nodes go with them; units the history places there are not moved.
lakeHints: Left-click to brush provinces · Right-drag or hold Space to move the map · Scroll to zoom · B brush · E eraser · [ ] brush size · Ctrl+Z to undo · Esc to leave
lakeWholeMore: {count} more states would be drowned whole
seaBrushHint: Land provinces you brush become sea, whole; they must touch the sea already there
seaEraserHint: Take back seas that are not saved yet
seaNote: Whole provinces become sea, joined to the sea already there (a lake does not count). Their victory points, buildings, railways and supply nodes go with them; the land around becomes coastal and can build ports. A country’s capital province and provinces where units start cannot become sea.
seaLandlocked: Province #{id} does not reach the sea: provinces made sea must touch the sea already there (a lake does not count)
seaLandlockedMore: {count} more do not reach the sea
landlessTitle: {count, plural, one {# state is} other {# states are}} only a lake, with no land for an air base and stronghold: the game crashes when a game starts. Click one to see it on the map:
repairBody: The game quits while loading a map with these. Fixing joins each cut-off sea to the sea region beside it and splits each state along region lines (the parts split off stay with the same country). Each state that is only a lake takes the land province beside it in the same strategic region, and that land's owner. You can undo it.
repairFixed: Fixed the map. You can undo this.

problem.busy: The map is being changed elsewhere. Try again in a few seconds.
problem.unreadable: The map files could not be read; nothing was changed.
problem.not_saved: This could not be saved; nothing was changed.
problem.bad_request: This change could not be read; nothing was changed. Undo it and try again.
problem.too_large: That is too much at once. Save it in smaller parts.
problem.own_map: This project’s own map files cannot be read, so they cannot be edited here. Re-import the mod and try again.
problem.no_country: There is no country {tag}. Create it first.
problem.state_drowned: {state} would be drowned whole: a state must keep at least one province.
problem.sea_divisions: {count, plural, one {# division starts} other {# divisions start}} in province #{id} and would have nowhere to stand. Move them to another province first.
problem.sea_capital: Province #{id} is the capital of {tags} ({state}) and cannot become sea.
problem.sea_unreached: Province #{id} does not reach the sea: provinces made sea must touch the sea already there (a lake does not count).
problem.sea_no_region: The sea beside province #{id} is in no strategic region, so the new sea has nowhere to join.
problem.region_empty: Every province of strategic region #{region} would become sea, leaving the region empty.
problem.sea_region_state: Sea region #{region} is cut apart; the cut-off part (province #{id} and others) holds only part of state #{state}, so it cannot join another region on its own.
problem.sea_region_alone: Sea region #{region} is cut apart; the cut-off part (province #{id}, {count} in all) has no other sea region beside it to join.
problem.land_breaks_map: The new land would break the map, so it was not saved.
problem.world_breaks_map: The map has errors, so it was not saved.
problem.undo_failed: This could not be undone; nothing was changed.
problem.nothing_to_undo: There is no map change to undo.
problem.water_terrain: Province #{id} is water; only land has a terrain to change.
problem.river_on_water: A river was drawn on water at ({x}, {y}).
problem.river_faults: This would join the rivers wrongly ({count, plural, one {# place} other {# places}}): sources at one end of a river, tributaries joining side by side, rivers one pixel wide.
problem.land_off_sea: The new land does not fall on the sea: new land can only be painted on the sea.
problem.land_outside_map: The new land must lie within the map ({width}×{height}) and be at least 4×4 pixels.
problem.land_covers_sea: Sea province #{id} would be almost covered by the new land (only {pixels} pixels left). Leave part of it: move or shrink the new land.
problem.upload_unreadable: {file} cannot be read; it must be a PNG or BMP.
problem.upload_jpeg: {file} cannot be a JPEG: lossy compression changes its colours. Use PNG or BMP.
problem.sketch_unreadable: The sketch cannot be read; it must be a PNG or JPEG.
problem.world_land_size: The province size must be between {min} and {max} pixels.
problem.world_per_state: Provinces per state must be between 1 and {max}.
problem.tag_invalid: A country is a three-letter tag such as GER (got {tag}).
problem.world_no_countries: Choose at least one country: the new world's states go to them.
problem.owners_not_png: The countries picture must be a PNG.
problem.owners_too_large: The countries picture is too large: at most {max} pixels.
problem.owners_extra_country: The countries picture has a country number {index}, but only {count} countries are chosen.
problem.world_country_unpainted: Country {tags} got no state: paint it some land on the map (covering most of a state), or remove it from the countries.
problem.world_size: The map pictures must be {width}×{height} (the base game's size); these are {got_width}×{got_height}.
problem.world_size_range: The map size is outside what can be made.
problem.world_no_land: There is no land on the map: it needs at least one piece of land.
problem.world_few_states: Only {states} states, not enough for {count} countries.
problem.upload_pictures_missing: The province, height and terrain maps are all needed.
problem.mod_state_gap: The MOD's state ids must run from 1 to {count} without a gap; #{missing} is missing.
problem.mod_state_no_land: These states of the MOD have no land (only lakes or sea, or no province on the province map), and the game quits when a game starts: {states}
problem.mod_state_capital: These states of the MOD have a capital that is not one of their own land provinces: {states}
problem.mod_needs_states_regions: Importing a MOD's map as it is needs its history/states (states) and map/strategicregions (strategic regions) files.
problem.mod_needs_definition: Importing a MOD's map as it is needs its map/definition.csv: its states are written by those province numbers.
problem.mod_file_outside: Only text files under map/strategicregions, history/states and localisation are taken from the MOD: {path}
problem.mod_too_many_files: Too many MOD files: at most {max}.
problem.mod_file_unreadable: A MOD file is too large or cannot be read: {path}
problem.mod_text_too_large: The MOD's text files are too large together.
problem.mod_unknown_tags: The MOD has countries the project does not have: make them first, or merge them into the project's countries.
problem.kind_land_water: This water province has no adjacent land state to join. Choose a state and strategic region, or use New land for an isolated island.
problem.kind_invalid: A province is land, sea or lake.
problem.lake_strands_coast: Making it a lake would leave these coastal provinces without sea, with nowhere for their ports: {provinces}
problem.water_continent: Sea and lakes belong to no continent.
problem.continent_range: The continent must be between 1 and {count}.
problem.state_land_only: Only land provinces belong to states.
problem.state_last_province: State #{state} has only this province; moving it would leave the state empty.
problem.state_last_land: State #{state} has only this land province left; moving it leaves only lakes, with nowhere for its air base and stronghold, and the game quits when a game starts.
problem.region_last_province: Strategic region #{region} has only this province; moving it would leave the region empty.
problem.region_file_text: The project's strategic region file {file} is not whole text, so it is not overwritten here.
problem.province_state_region: State #{state} has provinces in strategic region #{other}; province #{id} would be in #{region}. A state's provinces must be in one strategic region, or the game quits while loading the map.
problem.province_sea_split: This would cut the sea in {file} apart (province #{id} and others): a sea region must be in one piece, or the game quits while loading the map.
problem.other: The change could not be saved; nothing was changed.
problem.marked: The province it is about is marked red on the map.
problem.map_changed: This project’s map already has {count} changes (new land, province edits or an earlier new world). Restore the base map first, then create the whole world.
problem.map_changes_moved: The map changes no longer match the ones confirmed, so nothing was restored. Preview the new world again and confirm.
problem.imported_states: This project’s imported mod has its own states; a new world only works on projects without imported states.

finding.size_mismatch: The height, terrain or river map is not the size of the province map
finding.duplicate_color: Two provinces in definition.csv share a colour
finding.too_many_provinces: There may be more provinces than the game takes
finding.black_pixel: The province map has pure black pixels
finding.undefined_color: A colour on the province map is not in definition.csv
finding.unused_definition: A province in definition.csv has no pixels on the map
finding.disconnected_province: Some provinces are in separate pieces (the game reads this)
finding.province_box: Some provinces span more than the game allows
finding.x_crossing: Four provinces meet at a point somewhere (the game reads this)
finding.land_under_water: Some land provinces lie mostly below the water line
finding.water_above_land: Some sea or lake provinces lie mostly above the water line
finding.terrain_index: The terrain map uses a terrain the game does not define
finding.province_no_state: Some land provinces are in no state; the game quits while loading the map
finding.province_no_region: Some provinces are in no strategic region; the game quits while loading the map
finding.state_ids_gap: The state ids have a gap; the game quits while loading the map
finding.state_two_regions: Some states have provinces in more than one strategic region; the game quits while loading the map
finding.state_no_land: Some states are only a lake, with no land; the game quits when a game starts
finding.sea_region_split: Some sea regions are cut into separate pieces; the game quits while loading the map
finding.other: The map check found a problem

findingFix.size_mismatch: Export this picture again at the province map's size (the heightmap, terrain and river maps must all match it).
findingFix.duplicate_color: In definition.csv, give one of the provinces an unused colour and repaint it on the province map.
findingFix.duplicate_id: In definition.csv, change the repeated number to an unused one and check the state files that use it.
findingFix.black_pixel: Pure black is reserved and belongs to no province: merge these pixels into the provinces around them.
findingFix.undefined_color: These colours belong to no province: merge them into the provinces around them, or add a line for them in definition.csv.
findingFix.province_box: Split this province in two on the province map and add a line for the new part in definition.csv.
findingFix.province_no_state: Add these land provinces to a state (the provinces list of a state file).
findingFix.province_no_region: Add these provinces to a strategic region (provinces in map/strategicregions).
findingFix.state_ids_gap: State numbers must run from 1 without gaps: add the missing state files or renumber the later states.
findingFix.state_two_regions: Move this state's provinces into one strategic region, or split it into two states.
findingFix.state_no_land: This state has only lakes: give it a land province from a neighbouring state.
findingFix.sea_region_split: Make this sea region one connected area, or split it into several regions.

history.title: Map records ({count})
history.empty: The map is still the base game's: no records
history.undoLatestBody: “{name}” is undone and the map goes back to how it was before it.
history.restoreAllBody: All {count} map records are undone, new worlds and imported MOD maps too: the map, its states and strategic regions go back to the base game's. Countries and the project's other content stay.
history.restored: The base game's map is restored
history.moved: The map records just changed: the list is updated, confirm again
history.saveFirst: Save or discard your unsaved changes before undoing records
